title: Spectrum coordinates and comparison naturality for an affine square
statement: Let $X',X,S',S$ be affine schemes [def-pc-scheme] in a cartesian square $g',f',f,g$. Let $K,K'$ have quasi-coherent derived cohomology [def-pc-derived-category] and let $\phi:L(g')^*K\to K'$ [def-pc-derived-pullback]. Write $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and similarly for the other three schemes; each coordinate arrow is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the given arrow's global-section ring map. Fix a pullback proof for this coordinate square. There exist objects $K_0,K'_0$ with quasi-coherent cohomology and $\phi_0:L(g'_0)^*K_0\to K'_0$, such that the stalk condition [def-pc-single-complex-base-change-stalk-condition] for the coordinate data is equivalent to that for the original data. Write $b=\mathrm{BC}(K);Rf'_*\phi$ and $b_0=\mathrm{BC}_0(K_0);Rf'_{0*}\phi_0$ for the canonical comparisons [def-pc-derived-base-change-map] and [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. If $t:S'\to S'_0$ is the canonical spectrum isomorphism, there are endpoint isomorphisms $e_L:\operatorname{source}(b)\simeq Lt^*\operatorname{source}(b_0)$ and $e_R:\operatorname{target}(b)\simeq Lt^*\operatorname{target}(b_0)$ with $b=e_L;Lt^*(b_0);e_R^{-1}$. This asserts a commuting coordinate identification and does not assert invertibility of either comparison.

proof.text: Use the canonical isomorphisms of affine schemes to their global-section spectra. Naturality identifies the arrows with Spec.map of appTop; The supplied coordinate pullback proof agrees with the transported one by proof irrelevance. Pull back K and K′ along their inverse spectrum isomorphisms and use composition and identity comparisons to define phi0. Pullback preserves quasi-coherent cohomology.

The isomorphisms identify points, local rings and all four stalk maps. The natural tensor-pullback stalk isomorphisms and functoriality of the base derived tensor comparison identify the two canonical stalk comparisons. Changes of K-flat coordinates induce the same cohomology morphisms through the equations representing phi; hence the stalk conditions are equivalent.

The derived equivalences along the four spectrum isomorphisms and composition comparisons give the source and target identifications. Expand the canonical adjoint counit base-change construction: naturality of the counits and coherence of the pullback composition isomorphisms identify both paths, yielding the displayed equation. The zero ring and empty schemes are included by the same equivalences.

theorem exists_singleComplexAffineSpectrumCoordinates
    [∀ Y : Scheme.{u},
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    {X X' S S' : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (g : S' ⟶ S) (g' : X' ⟶ X)
    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    [IsAffine X] [IsAffine X'] [IsAffine S] [IsAffine S']
    (sq0 : IsPullback (Spec.map g'.appTop) (Spec.map f'.appTop)
      (Spec.map f.appTop) (Spec.map g.appTop))
    (K : schemeDerivedCategory X) (hK : schemeDerivedQCohProperty X K)
    (K' : schemeDerivedCategory X') (hK' : schemeDerivedQCohProperty X' K')
    (φ : (derivedPullback g').obj K ⟶ K') :
    let f0 := Spec.map f.appTop
    let f0' := Spec.map f'.appTop
    let g0 := Spec.map g.appTop
    let g0' := Spec.map g'.appTop
    ∃ (K0 : schemeDerivedCategory (Spec Γ(X, ⊤)))
      (K0' : schemeDerivedCategory (Spec Γ(X', ⊤)))
      (φ0 : (derivedPullback g0').obj K0 ⟶ K0'),
      schemeDerivedQCohProperty (Spec Γ(X, ⊤)) K0 ∧
      schemeDerivedQCohProperty (Spec Γ(X', ⊤)) K0' ∧
      (SingleComplexBaseChange.StalkCondition f f' g g' sq K K' φ ↔
        SingleComplexBaseChange.StalkCondition f0 f0' g0 g0' sq0 K0 K0' φ0) ∧
      ∃ (eL : (derivedPullback g).obj ((schemeDerivedDirectImage f).obj K) ≅
          (derivedPullback S'.toSpecΓ).obj
            ((derivedPullback g0).obj ((schemeDerivedDirectImage f0).obj K0)))
        (eR : (schemeDerivedDirectImage f').obj K' ≅
          (derivedPullback S'.toSpecΓ).obj ((schemeDerivedDirectImage f0').obj K0')),
        schemeDerivedBaseChangeMap f f' g g' sq.w K ≫
            (schemeDerivedDirectImage f').map φ =
          eL.hom ≫ (derivedPullback S'.toSpecΓ).map
            (schemeDerivedBaseChangeMap f0 f0' g0 g0' sq0.w K0 ≫
              (schemeDerivedDirectImage f0').map φ0) ≫ eR.inv
